To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
innate immune recognition of the commensal microbiota is required to maintain the symbiotic relationship between host and microbes.
innate immune receptors recognize bacterial products from the microbiota to promote host-microbial symbiotic interactions.
innate immune signaling is required for the long-term maintenance of host–microbiota symbiosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the innate immune system recognizes and responds to microbial symbionts to promote host-microbiota symbiosis.
the mechanisms that underlie the development of symbiotic relationships between the microbiota and the host.
understanding the molecular mechanisms that underlie the host's ability to recognize and respond to the microbiota.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
innate immune PRRs are critical in the maintenance of symbiotic relationships with the microbiota.
the immune system is not only an essential component for host defense against pathogens but also a critical component for host-microbial symbiotic relationships.
PRRs have evolved as sensors of both pathogen and host-derived molecules to mediate host responses to infection and to promote the establishment and long-term maintenance of host-microbial symbioses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the microbiota is an integral part of the innate immune system and that PRRs are required for the development and maintenance of host-microbial symbioses.
the innate immune system evolved to recognize the microbiota and promote host-microbial symbioses.
PRRs are required for the development of host tissue, and that they promote colonization by the microbiome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the microbiota is not just a bystander in the host but is actively shaping the host immune system.
the innate immune system has evolved to promote symbiotic relationships between host and microbiota.
innate immune recognition of the commensal microbiota is essential for the maintenance of host-microbial symbioses.
